problem.surface: PLP Pandora Android phone-local Qwen runtime
problem.symptom: Qwen prewarm started but navigating away from chat caused self_test failures with 'b00 was cancelled', so eligible turns fell back to Gemini.
problem.rootCause: AskPandoraScreen owned cancellation and unload of the process-shared PandoraLocalAi singleton in screen disposal/app lifecycle cleanup, so UI navigation could terminate an application-wide model warm.

implementation.approach: Move local-model residency and application lifecycle ownership to PandoraLocalAiRuntime at the app root. Screen navigation no longer cancels or unloads Qwen.
implementation.residencyPolicy: Keep a successfully warmed model resident across Pandora screens and cloud-only turns; use an application-scoped two-minute idle unload window.
implementation.teardownPolicy: Unload on app background/shutdown or explicit local-AI recovery/failure, not on route disposal.
implementation.regressionTest: Qwen residency is application-owned, not chat-screen-owned.

verification.note: Exact-source build and merge are verified; local token emission on the physical Redmi remains a post-install acceptance test.

coordinator.initialBlockReason: Required status check Pandora coordinator / integration was expected.

durableLessons: Shared phone-local models must have application-level lifetime ownership; individual screens must never own model residency.
Navigating between Pandora surfaces is not a reason to cancel or unload a warm local model.
Cloud fallback for one turn should preserve a healthy warm local model for the next eligible turn.
Exact-source CI can prove code/build integrity but cannot substitute for physical-phone token-generation acceptance.
For protected Pandora merges, satisfy the coordinator PASS and merge-fence contract rather than bypassing repository rules.
